cats: The spine of the pack — what to do next, and what you get for doing it.
Places that aren't the Overworld, each with its own progression.
What fills the map between the dimensions.
Everything that wants you dead, and the tools used to keep it balanced.
How fights actually play out, and what you carry into them.
Systems with their own rules, rituals and consequences.
Machines, logistics, rails, vehicles and where to put it all.
For when the fighting is done and the base still looks like a dirt hut.
Information, convenience and the small mercies.
Nothing to interact with. Libraries, loaders and the mods that keep the frame rate up.

mods.name: Better Questing
mods.desc: The questing engine the whole pack is built on. Quest lines, prerequisites, party support and reward chests, all driven from an in-game book.

mods.name: Standard Expansion
mods.desc: The task and reward library for Better Questing — retrieval, crafting, kill and location objectives, loot rewards, and the quest-line themes.

mods.name: Quest Book
mods.desc: Puts the quest interface on a physical book you carry, so you can open your quest log without a keybind or a command.

mods.name: QuestForge Content
mods.desc: The pack's own mod: 81 custom enchantments with their own application rules, a proximity voice chat, a working in-game jukebox, and the survey tools used to balance the pack.

mods.name: Level Up!
mods.desc: An RPG skill tree layered over vanilla. Spend levels on Mining, Sword, Archery and more, or pick a class; a Book of Unlearning lets you respec.

mods.name: Loot Bags
mods.desc: Mobs drop sealed pouches instead of only their usual loot. Open one for a weighted roll from a pack-wide loot table.

mods.name: The Twilight Forest
mods.desc: A permanently dusk-lit forest dimension gated behind a progression of bosses — the Naga, the Lich, the Hydra — each one unlocking the next region.

mods.name: Hardcore Ender Expansion
mods.desc: Rebuilds the End into a real destination: a genuinely difficult Ender Dragon, new biomes and ores, endermen that behave, and a reward worth the fight.

mods.name: Welcome to the Jungle
mods.desc: Overhauls jungle biomes with dense new growth, dinosaurs, and jungle-specific gear and structures.

mods.name: Chocolate Quest
mods.desc: Large hand-designed dungeons — castles, pyramids, ships, walled towns — filled with scripted humanoid bosses and their loot. Formerly Better Dungeons.

mods.name: Roguelike Dungeons
mods.desc: Multi-floor dungeons that get harder and richer the deeper you go, ending in a boss room. Generated fresh every world.

mods.name: Doomlike Dungeons
mods.desc: Sprawling multi-room complexes generated in the style of classic Doom levels — themed rooms, locked routes and spawner clusters.

mods.name: Recurrent Complex
mods.desc: The structure engine behind much of the pack's worldgen. Places custom villages, ruins and set-pieces, and can import or export any build.

mods.name: Lycanites Mobs
mods.desc: A full bestiary keyed to biome and element — every environment gets its own set of predators, plus tameable mounts, summonable pets and elemental bosses.

mods.name: Mutant Creatures
mods.desc: Mini-boss versions of the vanilla mobs. The Mutant Creeper, Enderman and Zombie all hit far harder than the originals and drop trophies worth having.

mods.name: TragicMC 2
mods.desc: Its own progression of mobs, bosses and dimensions, leaning hard into large multi-stage boss fights.

mods.name: OreSpawn
mods.desc: Enormous creatures, royal dragons, new dimensions and joke-scale weapons. Loud, chaotic, and the source of several of the pack's late-game targets.

mods.name: Infernal Mobs
mods.desc: Diablo-style rare modifiers on ordinary mobs. A random zombie can roll Vengeance, Sprint and Ender — much deadlier, and much better loot.

mods.name: Custom NPCs
mods.desc: The tool behind the pack's named characters: questgivers, shopkeepers and dialogue trees, all authored in-game.

mods.name: Mob Properties
mods.desc: Rewrites any mob's drops, attributes and NBT from config — the lever used to retune spawns and loot across every mob mod at once.

mods.name: Just Another Spawner
mods.desc: Takes over vanilla spawning so a dozen mob mods can share a world without one of them flooding every biome.

mods.name: Colorful Mobs
mods.desc: Dye any living thing. Comes with a colour wand, invisibility powder and rainbow dust for the ones you can't reach.

mods.name: Lucky Egg
mods.desc: An egg that summons something. Occasionally that something is survivable.

mods.name: Killer Pacman
mods.desc: Adds Pacman as a hostile mob, plus a block that keeps him away from wherever you'd rather he wasn't.

mods.name: Mine & Blade: Battlegear 2
mods.desc: Real dual-wielding, shields with a block stance, quivers, and a sheath system that puts your weapons on your back.

mods.name: Soul Shards: The Old Ways
mods.desc: Bind the souls of the mobs you kill to a shard, then cash a full shard in for a controllable spawner. The classic soul-cage grind.

mods.name: Baubles
mods.desc: Adds ring, amulet and belt slots to the inventory. Several mods in the pack put their best passive gear in them.

mods.name: Adventure Backpack
mods.desc: Wearable backpacks with built-in fluid tanks, a sleeping bag and tool slots. Each variant is themed to the mob or biome it's made from.

mods.name: Damage Indicators
mods.desc: Floating damage numbers and a boss-style health bar for whatever you're currently hitting, with its name and active potion effects.

mods.name: Mob Amputation
mods.desc: Limbs come off when you hit hard enough, and the mob keeps coming without them.

mods.name: Mob Dismemberment
mods.desc: The gorier companion to Mob Amputation — mobs come apart on death rather than politely vanishing.

mods.name: Witchery
mods.desc: A deep witchcraft system: cauldron brewing, ritual circles, broomsticks, voodoo poppets, lycanthropy and vampirism, and demons that notice you meddling.

mods.name: ProjectE
mods.desc: The modern rewrite of Equivalent Exchange 2 — EMC values, transmutation tables and the Philosopher's Stone line all the way up.

mods.name: Pandora's Box
mods.desc: One box, hundreds of possible effects, no way to know which you'll get. Ranges from a free diamond to a localised apocalypse.

mods.name: Lucky Blocks
mods.desc: Break the block and roll the dice: loot, structures, mob ambushes or something considerably worse.

mods.name: Psychedelicraft
mods.desc: Brewing, distilling and the substances that follow, with genuinely elaborate shader-driven visual effects.

mods.name: Sync
mods.desc: Build a body-swap shell and store a copy of yourself in it. Die anywhere and wake up in the shell with your inventory intact.

mods.name: Legends Mod
mods.desc: Five packs in one — Superheroes, Star Wars, Kaiju, Horror and Battlebourn — each with its own characters, suits, bosses and gear.

mods.name: Transformers
mods.desc: Transformable vehicles and characters, built from the FiskFille original and rebuilt locally for this pack.

mods.name: TARDIS Mod
mods.desc: A working TARDIS: bigger on the inside, flyable between dimensions, with a console room you upgrade over time.

mods.name: Weeping Angels
mods.desc: They only move when you aren't looking. Blink and you're somewhere else entirely.

mods.name: Portal Gun
mods.desc: The Aperture Science handheld portal device, with companion cubes, turrets, hard light bridges and long fall boots.

mods.name: Gravity Gun
mods.desc: Pick up, hold and launch almost anything — blocks, mobs, other players. The supercharged variant disintegrates what it grabs.

mods.name: MC Helicopter
mods.desc: Flyable helicopters, jets and tanks with working weapon systems and a proper cockpit view.

mods.name: Railcraft
mods.desc: The definitive rail mod: real track switching and signalling, steam and electric locomotives, tunnel bores, coke ovens and blast furnaces.

mods.name: ICBM Classic
mods.desc: Missiles, launch platforms, radar and remote detonators, from small tactical rockets up to warheads you should not use near your base.

mods.name: Voltz Engine
mods.desc: The engine layer ICBM runs on, providing its energy system, multiblocks and world-edit handling.

mods.name: Compact Machines
mods.desc: Cubes that hold a whole room inside. Walk in through a tunnel and build a full factory in a space one block wide.

mods.name: Ender Utilities
mods.desc: Ender-themed logistics: linked storage, remote inventory access, teleport tools and a builder's wand set.

mods.name: OpenBlocks
mods.desc: A grab bag that turned out to be essential — elevators, hang gliders, sponges, tanks, trophies, the golden eye, and a sprinkler.

mods.name: Archimedes' Ships Plus
mods.desc: Build a vessel out of ordinary blocks, attach a helm, and sail or fly the whole thing as one moving object.

mods.name: Storage Drawers
mods.desc: Wall-mounted drawers that each hold one item type in bulk, with the contents shown on the front. The pack's default bulk storage.

mods.name: Iron Chest
mods.desc: The chest upgrade ladder — iron, gold, diamond, crystal — each step wider than the last, upgradeable in place.

mods.name: Ender Storage
mods.desc: Colour-coded chests and tanks that share one inventory across any distance or dimension.

mods.name: Chest Transporter
mods.desc: Pick up a full chest and carry it somewhere else without unpacking it first.

mods.name: Hopper Ducts
mods.desc: Hoppers that move items sideways and upward, for item routing that doesn't need a tech mod.

mods.name: ChickenChunks
mods.desc: Chunk loaders with a map interface, so your farms and quarries keep running while you're elsewhere.

mods.name: Wireless Redstone
mods.desc: Redstone signals sent by frequency instead of wire, with handheld remotes and receiver blocks.

mods.name: SecurityCraft
mods.desc: Keypads, retinal scanners, laser grids, cameras and mines — everything needed to make a base genuinely annoying to rob.

mods.name: Chisel 2
mods.desc: Dozens of alternate textures for nearly every building block, cycled with a single chisel tool.

mods.name: Carpenter's Blocks
mods.desc: Slopes, stairs, doors and beds that take on the texture of whatever block you cover them with.

mods.name: ArchitectureCraft
mods.desc: Rounded and angled architectural shapes — arches, domes, cladding and window frames — cut from any material.

mods.name: BiblioCraft
mods.desc: Display and organisation furniture: bookcases, tool racks, weapon cases, potion shelves, desks, map frames and labelled storage.

mods.name: Decocraft
mods.desc: Over 500 detailed props — kitchenware, instruments, plush toys, tools and clutter — for dressing an interior.

mods.name: MrCrayfish's Furniture Mod
mods.desc: Working household furniture: fridges that store food, cookers, televisions, showers and blinds.

mods.name: Malisis' Doors
mods.desc: Animated doors, trapdoors, garage doors, sliding panels and a working elevator, all with proper opening animations.

mods.name: Statues
mods.desc: A hammer that carves large decorative statues from ordinary building blocks.

mods.name: Mob Statues
mods.desc: Poseable statues of the mobs themselves, for trophies and displays.

mods.name: The SecretRoomsMod
mods.desc: Camouflaged blocks, one-way glass and hidden levers for building doors nobody else can find.

mods.name: Hats
mods.desc: A large wardrobe of cosmetic hats that also show up on mobs you meet.

mods.name: Hat Stand
mods.desc: A poseable stand for displaying the hats you've collected.

mods.name: JourneyMap
mods.desc: The pack's map: live minimap, full-screen world map, waypoints and mob radar, mapped as you explore. Bound to [J].

mods.name: Waila
mods.desc: Shows what you're looking at and which mod it came from, in a tooltip at the top of the screen.

mods.name: Not Enough Items
mods.desc: The recipe browser. Search every item in the pack, view its recipe and its uses, and see what it's used for.

mods.name: NEI Addons
mods.desc: Extra NEI panels for mods that ship their own crafting and villager trading systems.

mods.name: NEI Integration
mods.desc: Fills in NEI recipe handlers for mods that never wrote their own.

mods.name: Inventory Tweaks
mods.desc: One-key inventory and chest sorting, plus automatic replacement of a tool or stack the moment it runs out.

mods.name: Controlling
mods.desc: Makes the controls screen searchable — necessary once a hundred mods have all claimed a keybind.

mods.name: No More Recipe Conflict
mods.desc: When two mods claim the same recipe shape, this lets you cycle between the results instead of always getting one.

mods.name: Gravestones
mods.desc: Death drops your inventory into a grave at the spot instead of scattering it across the floor to despawn.

mods.name: Custom Menu
mods.desc: Drives the pack's custom title screen — its background, layout and menu music.

mods.name: Sound Filters
mods.desc: Adds reverb in caves and muffles sound underwater and through walls. Small change, large effect underground.

mods.name: Fast Leaf Decay
mods.desc: Leaves decay in seconds after you fell a tree instead of hanging around for minutes.

mods.name: Inventory Pets
mods.desc: Living pets that sit in your inventory and grant a passive effect as long as you keep them fed.

mods.name: Food Plus
mods.desc: A large spread of new dishes, drinks and ingredients, with the crops and cooking gear to make them.

mods.name: Food Expansion
mods.desc: More recipes for the food already in the game, so ordinary ingredients have somewhere to go.

mods.name: Origin
mods.desc: A small addition that puts lamb chops on the menu, raw and cooked, under its own Country Gamer tab.

mods.name: Trail Mix
mods.desc: A snack that grants a random temporary skill — a fireball, a jump boost — for as long as the effect lasts.

mods.name: FastCraft
mods.desc: The single biggest frame-rate gain in the pack. Optimises chunk rendering and world ticking with no gameplay change.

mods.name: BetterFps
mods.desc: Swaps in faster maths routines for the hot paths in the render loop.

mods.name: OptiFine
mods.desc: Render settings, connected textures, dynamic lights and the video options needed to tune the pack to your machine.

mods.name: AI Improvements
mods.desc: Cuts the cost of mob pathfinding, which matters when this many mob mods are loaded at once.

mods.name: Chunk Pregenerator
mods.desc: Generates world chunks ahead of time so exploring doesn't stutter while worldgen catches up.

mods.name: MobiusCore
mods.desc: Core hooks used for server profiling and diagnostics.

mods.name: CraftTweaker
mods.desc: Lets the pack add, remove and rewrite recipes by script — how the pack's crafting tree is kept coherent across a hundred mods.

mods.name: ModTweaker 2
mods.desc: Extends CraftTweaker's reach to mod-specific machines and rituals.

mods.name: QuestForge Tweaks
mods.desc: The pack's own coremod — two bytecode patches, one for the quest panel UI and one for menu music control.

mods.name: CodeChicken Core
mods.desc: Loader and patching layer required by NEI and the ChickenBones mods.

mods.name: CodeChicken Lib
mods.desc: Shared rendering and utility code for the ChickenBones mods.

mods.name: Forge Multipart
mods.desc: Lets several separate parts — cables, covers, panels — occupy one block space.

mods.name: CodingLib
mods.desc: Support library for the Legends Mod.

mods.name: OpenMods Lib
mods.desc: Shared framework behind OpenBlocks.

mods.name: iChunUtil
mods.desc: Shared library for Portal Gun, Gravity Gun, Hats, Sync and the dismemberment mods.

mods.name: AnimationAPI
mods.desc: Model animation framework used by Mutant Creatures and others.

mods.name: IvToolkit
mods.desc: Shared toolkit for Recurrent Complex and Pandora's Box.

mods.name: MalisisCore
mods.desc: Rendering and GUI framework behind Malisis' Doors.

mods.name: asielib
mods.desc: Small utility library used by Computronics-family mods.

mods.name: Dark Core
mods.desc: Core functionality for the DarkCraft mods.

mods.name: Moving World
mods.desc: The physics layer that lets Archimedes' Ships move built structures with their tile entities intact.

mods.name: Saintscore
mods.desc: Core file and pack loader for the Saints content packs.

mods.name: MMMLib
mods.desc: Model and multi-model support library for the Little Maid mods.
